modules.module_title: Conducting pre-operation checks and routine maintenance of the Loader

pcs.pc_description: follow the work related instructions given by the supervisor before the shift starts
check oil levels of engine, transmission, differential, hydraulic tank etc. and top up as required
check water level in the radiator and top up as required

confirm availability and functionality of safety features in the Loader like audiovisual alarm, reverse camera, mirrors, horn, seat belt, Roll-Over Protection Structure (ROPS) and Falling Object Protective Structure (FOPS)
check fan belt tension, electrolyte level and batteries’ terminal tightness
clean the Loader and outer element of air cleaner with compressed air
apply grease to all the required parts
drain accumulated water from the diesel tank
check air pressure in tyres for tyre mounted Loader and track's tension for track mounted Loader and take action as required
take action as per the entries done by the previous operator in the Loader logbook
check for any spills/leakages in the engine, hydraulic systems, transmission etc.
plug spill, leakage of oil and lubricants and escalate to appropriate authority if unable to rectify
check functioning of fire extinguishers, automatically operated fire suppression system and devices including fire detection system in the Loader
clean air filter dust bowls
check the gasket and inner filter element
inspect the body components like Loader's frame and arm for any cracks or wear and tear
check the bucket cutting edge and the bucket for excessive damage, if any
inspect all mounting bolts, pivot pins and ram pins
clean any muck, soil or debris from the area around the slewing rams
examine the various controls, gauges, warning lamps
check and adjust driving position, rear and side mirrors, seat belts and confirm clear uninterrupted vision all around
inspect the work site before commencement of operation

pcs.pc_description: use Loader in an optimum way as per the instruction manual
start the engine by using push button and key switch together
use the priming pump and pre-heater to start the engine in cold weather conditions
ensure that no other operators travel on or stand near the Loader
check backhoe/ front hoe is in transport position while the loader is moving
select correct gear range by shifting the quadrant device
inspect critical temperature and pressure gauges during driving
use various signalling devices available in the Loader such as turn signal, parking indicator, air horn etc. as per requirement
keep a safe distance from the tip edge and use an approved stop block/safety parapet before tipping over an edge
park the Loader safely and appropriately
select and use the right kind of brake in different situations and working conditions
stop the engine of Loader by following Standard Operating Procedure (SOP)
follow manufacturer’s instructions for safe operation and durability of the Loader
deploy the digger stabilizer legs to level the Loader when working on a slope
maintain stability and anchorage during digging operation, by using the loader's arms
manoeuver the joystick lever provided for backhoe operations
operate the four levers to control the digging arm, dipper arm and stabilizer legs
discharge the load safely at the designated place
ensure that backhoe is never utilised for craning
inform supervisor of problems while operating the Loader

pcs.pc_description: track machine operating hours to assess the required service
park the Loader on a firm and level ground before attempting to carry out any maintenance activity
inspect the tyre rims, air pressure, wheel nuts and treads for tyre-mounted Loader or track chain tension, track motor, roller for track-mounted Loader

fill the daily, weekly and monthly maintenance/defect sheets as per the format laid down by the organization
ensure that no diagnosis on the machine is performed when it is running or is still hot
identify fault in the Loader and trace the cause of this fault
check the instrument panel and control gauge to identify out of range readings to find the defect/cause of failure
conduct scheduled, routine examination and assessments against equipment specifications to identify wear, damage, corrosion, inadequate fluid levels, leaks and general condition and serviceability
carry out diagnostic procedures as per the troubleshooting checklist prepared by the Original Equipment Manufacturer (OEM)
assess the problem when it is beyond one's competence and report the problem to concerned person
follow standard operating procedure set out for diagnosing faults
review complaint sheet, logbook and history sheet of the equipment to identify the repair requirements
follow "5-S" practice near the workshop area

modules.module_title: Follow work-site health and safety measures

pcs.pc_description: comply with safety, health, and security- related regulations/guidelines at the opencast mine
follow the safety instructions given by the workman's inspector
follow adequate safety while working at haul roads, heights, overburden dumps, sump area, stockyard, near moving parts, etc.
take safety precautions while working on sites (sub-station, workshop etc.), with equipment, and conducting welding and cutting operations
follow appropriate Safe Operating Procedure (SOP) while dealing with explosives
respond promptly and appropriately to an accident/ incident or an emergency situation, within limits of the role and responsibility
provide first aid to an injured person
operate various types of fire extinguishers to control different types of fire at a worksite when required
use appropriate PPE as per the requirement
maintain hand hygiene by washing hands with alcohol based sanitisers/soap
disinfect the machine/tools before and after work/task
maintain hygiene at the work site
report any symptoms of illness to the shift- incharge
identify the environmental impact of related opencast mining operations
follow the process for collecting, storing and disposing of the hazardous material and waste (like used oil, lubricant, battery, etc.) in compliance with worksite guidelines
ensure not to mix topsoil with waste in day to day tasks
ensure that HEMM is washed at the designated location
ensure the productivity of the machine for material/fuel conservation
follow the mineral conservation practices specified by the organization in accordance with MCDR-2017 (Mineral Conservation and Development Rules)
assist supervisor for reducing environmental impact caused due to related mining operations
